conjugation of minor groove binders with oligonucleotides enhances DNA duplex and tripe stability.
conjugation of minor groove binders to oligonucleotides increases their affinity to DNA and RNA and can be applied for stabilization of DNA double and triple helices.
the conjugation of two parallel or antiparellel minor groove binders to the same oligonucleotide phosphate group results in the stabilization of DNA duplex and triple helices.

the design and synthesis of novel conjugates that can be used for stabilization of DNA structures.
the development of the new approach to the stabilization of DNA structures by conjugation of MGBs to oligonucleotides.
the synthesis of conjugates containing two MGB attached to the same phosphate group of one oligonucloetide strand and their interaction with DNA and DNA triplexes.

MGB conjugation to oligonucleotides is a powerful method for the stabilization of DNA duplex and triple helices and can be used in the design of oligonucleotide-based drugs.
the binding affinity of conjugated MGA to DNA is significantly higher than that of individual MGB, and that the binding of the conjugate is sequence specific.
the MGBs conjugation to oligonucleotides is a very efficient way for stabilization of DNA double and triple helices.

the conjugation of MGB to oligonucleotides increases stability of both DNA and RNA duplexes, and of DNA triplexes.
